correctness.rationale: In finite downset representation J(P), neg A={p:↓p∩A=empty}. Failure of neg(A∩B)=neg A ∪neg B has a witness p above two different minimal points split between disjoint traces. The injection A↦(A,neg A) gives b>=u. Equality forces exactly two minima and every other poset point above both: a third minimal point or nonminimal point above just one gives two distinct bad partners for an already unary-bad coordinate. Conversely in A2⊕Q only the two ordered singleton cross pairs fail, while Ak⊕Q has disjoint nonempty proper subset pairs counted 3^k−2^(k+1)+1. At h>=5 the bound and chain Q witnesses are sharp. Independently computed all naturally labeled posets through 5 points (407), checking direct pseudocomplements, b>=u, equality characterization.
residual_risks: Universally equivalent qualitative Stone equations do not imply numerical equality; sampling is ordered pairs with replacement. Exhaustive finite n<=5 is supplementary to all-size downset argument.
